summary: Phase 149O.18A -- HATP Mandatory Cutover State Foundation: bounded implementation phase (Wave A of the 149O.17 plan). Ran the required initial inspection and confirmed baseline: repo clean, origin/main..HEAD=0, 149O.17 completed/complete, HMRC-001 v1.0 VERIFIED WITH NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS -- CONFORMS, HATP production NOT READY, runtime Observed/observe/unavailable. Read HMRC-001 in full, the 149O.17 implementation plan in full (especially Section 9.1's Wave A module design), hatp_bootstrap.py and repository_identity.py in full, and hatp_ag_authority.py's production-repository-context precedent, then directly reconfirmed HATPTrustStore.production().root (hatp_bootstrap.py:528-537) is the existing public protected-root accessor this phase reuses unmodified. Added the sole new production module src/pcae/core/hatp_mandatory_cutover.py: the CutoverMode(str, Enum) vocabulary (LEGACY_COMPATIBLE/PREPARED/HATP_MANDATORY, no fourth mode value anywhere); the closed-schema CutoverRecord model/parser (strict isinstance(int)-and-not-bool version guard, duplicate-JSON-key rejection mirroring existing repository precedent, a new Z-suffix-only fully-anchored strict timestamp grammar matching cltr/authority/envelope.py's existing precedent for a new authority-bearing field rather than either existing permissive fromisoformat-based parser); protected persistence under HATPTrustStore.production().root with no modification to hatp_bootstrap.py and a locally-duplicated two-line symlink-rejection helper (both target and parent checked); the fresh-every-call mode-resolution algorithm implementing exactly the 149O.17 Section 9.1 decision tree (first-install, valid record, wrong-repository treated as not-present-for-this-repo, deleted/corrupt/unknown-version/boolean-version record all fail-closed to HATP_MANDATORY via monotonic-marker consultation, corrupt marker never treated as absent to prevent a corruption-triggered downgrade, a genuinely-unreachable corrupt-record-with-no-marker case treated as an internal-consistency fail-closed outcome per the plan's own step-5 disposition); the separate write-once monotonic activation-history marker (O_CREAT|O_EXCL, deliberately distinct from the record's own os.replace forward-transition semantics); and centralized transition-graph validation (only LEGACY_COMPATIBLE->PREPARED and PREPARED->HATP_MANDATORY permitted; every reverse transition, every direct skip, and PREPARED->LEGACY_COMPATIBLE -- not frozen either way by HMRC-001 and therefore deliberately omitted, not guessed -- all rejected or inexpressible). Resolved the 149O.17 plan's deferred admin-authority-mechanism question by direct source reading: confirmed no application-level Protected-Activation-Authority principal/check type exists anywhere in this codebase (HATPTrustStore itself is deliberately read-only; the 149O.6/149O.7 lineage's actual Class-B mechanism is OS-principal-separation, not an in-process object) and therefore did not invent one -- the internal transition writer (_write_cutover_transition) takes an explicit protected_root parameter and is never paired, anywhere in the module, with HATPTrustStore.production().root (confirmed by an AST-based, not substring-based, single-call-site test), relying on the same OS-level file-permission boundary the sibling registry.json already relies on. Implemented real concurrent-transition-safety via fcntl.flock plus a fresh mode re-resolution immediately before write (TOCTOU discipline), verified with real threading-based concurrency tests (identical-transition races and PREPARED-vs-HATP_MANDATORY races), not merely asserted. Authored 114 new tests across two files (85 in tests/test_hatp_mandatory_cutover.py covering the full model/parser/resolution/transition/concurrency surface including attacks 22/39/40/41/42; 29 in tests/test_phase_149o_18a_hatp_mandatory_cutover_state_foundation.py covering the production-file allowlist, contract byte-identity, AST-based dependency-closure and protected-root-usage checks, and no-real-activation confirmations), both added to Fast Green (deterministic, filesystem-only, no hardware/network/wall-clock dependency). Ran a full HMRC/HATP/rollback/PB regression sweep and, via a true isolated git-worktree baseline checkout at the phase-entering commit (not a partial checkout, which does not delete files absent from the target commit), independently confirmed every resulting failure is either pre-existing at the 149O.17 baseline and unrelated to this phase, or a necessary, well-understood, HMRC-001-wave-sequencing consequence of this phase's required production module now existing (historical no-file-exists-yet/no-src-pcae-changed-since-my-own-entry-commit snapshot assertions in five older phase-verification test files) -- no AG3/AG5/rollback/Permission-Broker behavioral regression was found in any sweep (permission-broker suite 234/234 passed; rollback-focused agent suite 78/78 passed). VERDICT: HATP MANDATORY CUTOVER STATE FOUNDATION: IMPLEMENTED -- READY FOR 149O.18B. No evidence consumption, no AG3/AG5 gating, no CLI plumbing, no legacy-authority change, no Permission Broker change, and no real HATP_MANDATORY activation of the current deployment. HMRC-001 v1.0 and all six upstream contracts remain byte-unchanged. B-149O-1..4 remain INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED AT HATP-GATED AUTHORITY BOUNDARY -- SYSTEM EXECUTION CLOSURE DEFERRED. HATP production remains NOT READY. Runtime remains Observed / observe / unavailable. Recommended next phase: 149O.18B -- HATP Mandatory Evidence Consumption Adapter.

validation_results.result: New (149O.18A, informational): HMRC-REQ-043/048's single, flat, host-level Cutover Record location necessarily means the monotonic marker inherits the same shared-single-slot topology; on a host running more than one repository against the same protected root, a wrong-repository marker cannot affirmatively prove first-install status.
